wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: library API with no HTTP status; the stated refusal form is an error raised to the caller, so a crash and a clean refusal are the same observable and this class adds no separate guarantee
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected thing is the destination address of the read itself, not a neighbouring or proxy resource
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the destination is resolved against the response before it is validated, and no normalising or adjusting step sits between validation and the request
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity, role or credential parsing decides the guard in this task
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority or secret lookup exists whose empty answer could fail open

traps.shape: credentials forwarded across origins; requests strips only Authorization, so API-key/token headers and the cookies argument still reach the second origin
traps.realistic_because: requests itself strips only the Authorization header on a host change; custom API-key/token headers and the cookies argument survive a cross-origin redirect in the real client (verified on the pinned tree)

traps.shape: the same requests.get-after-validate_url shape in the lower-level content loaders and the shared URL helper, whose starting URL is validated by the caller
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the caller-level validation of the starting URL makes the loaders look already protected

traps.pattern: B route where the protection never existed
traps.shape: a result link supplied by a third-party search response is fetched with requests.get and redirects enabled, with no URL validation at all

traps.pattern: injected sibling (route where the protection never existed)
traps.shape: a direct fetch of the caller's URL behind an error branch, after the function has already validated the starting URL
traps.realistic_because: a fallback-on-failure fetch is a common maintainer addition; the validate_url at the top of the function makes the whole function read as handled

traps.pattern: injected sibling (different verb on a metadata path)
traps.shape: a content-type probe sends a HEAD request with redirects enabled before the download
traps.realistic_because: type sniffing before a download is a natural loader feature and HEAD looks like a harmless metadata read

traps.pattern: injected sibling (fetch created from content already read)
traps.shape: a requests.Session fetch of navigation links found in the fetched page
traps.realistic_because: the loader already collects and resolves navigation links for its output; fetching them is the obvious next feature, and a Session keeps it off the requests.get path
